_comment: Perceived-latency budgets for gateway-backed flows, stated from the vault owner's seat. The gateway's MACHINE-cost budgets (request p99, RSS, event-loop lag, fsyncs per write, idle churn) already live in packages/server/benchmarks/low-end-budgets.json and stay there — this file is the symptom layer above them. See README.md for the status vocabulary and the year-3 volume table. Ratcheted tighten-only via PERF_BUDGET_SOURCES.

sendToFirstToken.volume: empty vault, no conversation history — 13 runs of 25-30 sampled turns, each after 5 discarded warmups, provider held constant at zero think time
sendToFirstToken.probe: scripts/perf/send-to-first-token.mjs — drives a real runAcpTurn against the scripted packages/server/src/acp/backends/acp/fake-acp-harness.mjs (--mode=normal) and times t0 (send) → first `assistant.delta`. PARTIAL BY CONSTRUCTION, and this entry says so rather than implying the whole interval is fenced. IN the span: harness process spawn, the ACP initialize handshake, session/new, session/prompt dispatch, and the stream translation in packages/server/src/acp/backends/acp/backend.ts. OUT of it: the HTTP/SSE conversation route in front of runAcpTurn, every client (no renderer, no frame, no composer), and a real provider's own time to first token — that last one is deliberately excluded, because it is the provider's number and not a regression this repo can fix. STILL UNMEASURED: the route + client half, which needs the desktop/web e2e mock gateway to serve a fixed-delay SSE turn plus a client-side first-token marker to observe; the `sendToFirstToken` entries in desktop.json and web.json remain unmeasured for exactly that reason.

_provenance.host: linux x64, 4 cpus, shared container under concurrent sibling load (load average 3.3-4.5 of 4 during the noisiest runs); @centraid/server consumed from its built dist
_provenance.note: MEASURED — and what it replaces is NO NUMBER AT ALL. Before this the product's most-felt latency had no rig: tests/perf/harness-turn.perf.test.ts measures 2,000 registry dispatches against a stubbed runTurn, so it never spawns a harness, never speaks ACP, and could not see this interval. The stub the old probe text asked for turned out to already exist (fake-acp-harness.mjs, the ACP backend suite's fixture); the missing piece was a rig pointing at it. Thirteen independent runs of 25-30 samples put per-run p95 between 53.4 ms on an idle container and 123.0 ms under concurrent load, while the per-run MEDIAN barely moved (47.9-69.5 ms) — so the spread is host contention on the process spawn, not variance in the path itself. Every observed* value above records the WORST run seen, never the friendliest. The number is dominated by node process spawn plus the JSON-RPC handshake, which is the honest shape of a first turn. READ IT AS A LOWER BOUND on what the vault owner feels: it fences a gateway-side regression — a slower spawn, an added handshake round trip, a blocking step inserted before the prompt goes out — not the whole perceived interval.
_provenance.headroom: ~3.3x worst observed p95 (~2x the worst single sample), in the same grammar as requestToFirstByte above. Sized against the CONTENDED measurement on purpose, because a shared CI runner IS the contended case: a ceiling seeded from the idle 53 ms p95 would fence runner jitter rather than a regression, and a gate that flakes is a gate that gets widened. The ratchet is tighten-only, so this can only come DOWN — re-seed it from a real distribution on the lane that runs it.

reconnectToFresh.probe: NONE TODAY. tests/scale/replica-bootstrap.scale.test.ts measures a windowed bootstrap with an in-flight deletion, which is the closest existing signal; the perceived number needs the change-stream resume path timed from disconnect to first correct frame.
reconnectToFresh._blockedOn: BLOCKED-EXTERNAL (#842 register): no harness times the change-stream resume path from disconnect to first correct frame at the 50,000-replica-row volume; the existing replica-bootstrap scale rig measures a windowed bootstrap, not reconnect staleness. Per tests/experience-budgets/README.md, `unmeasured` with this loud probe is the sanctioned honest state — it carries NO ceiling and gates nothing by design, and no number is invented here. Unblocking is a harness slice: time the resume path, then seed `ceilingMs` and flip status to `measured`.

_provenance.host: darwin arm64, gateway in a forked child (tests/perf/fixtures/gateway-idle-server.mjs)
_provenance.note: Pre-existing measurement, restated here in owner terms and NOT re-derived. Ceiling is ~3x observed. The volume is EMPTY — this number says nothing about a year-3 vault, and the honest reading is that it fences a transport regression, not a scale one. packages/server/benchmarks/low-end-budgets.json holds the matching machine-cost ceiling (requestP99Ms 250) for the low-end host profile.

coreRouteP95Ms.volume: empty vault, 30 serial requests per core route identity

gatewayColdStartMs.volume: fork to authenticated ready message, empty vault

year3RestoreSeconds.volume: 10 GiB of CAS bytes + 95,640 FK-checked rows (90,640 core_content_item + 5,000 core_party)

_provenance.note: MEASURED — this replaces a guess. Before #659 the largest restore the repo had ever executed was ~160 MiB, and the year-3 restore time was unmeasured. A 10 GiB vault comes back in 55 s on local NVMe. CI disks and a network provider are materially slower, hence a ceiling of ~3x observed. NOTE the asymmetry: taking the snapshot costs 152 s, nearly 3x the restore — chunking + AEAD on the way in is the expensive direction.
_provenance.headroom: ~3.2x observed (local-disk measurement, CI/network provider will be slower)

restoreForeignKeyCheckMs.volume: 95,640 rows in the restored vault.db (73 MB file), year-3 row counts
restoreForeignKeyCheckMs.probe: tests/scale/restore-10gib.scale.test.ts — timed alone on a freshly opened connection so neither pragma warms the other's page cache

_provenance.note: MEASURED, and the answer is reassuring: foreign_key_check — the O(rows) full-table walk that packages/backup/src/wal-restore.ts runs inside every restore, and the suspected year-3 cliff — costs 21 ms at year-3 row volume. integrity_check is 37x more expensive at 785 ms, and BOTH together are ~1.5% of the 55 s restore. The honesty check in the restore path is not the thing to optimise. Ceiling is generous on purpose: it fences a genuine cliff (a missing parent index turning the walk quadratic), not runner jitter.

fiveVaultFootprint.volume: 5 mounted vaults = 10 SQLite handles (year-3 household: Personal auto-founded per #603, plus one shared or personal vault per member)

_provenance.note: MEASURED. The reservations are now FLAT in vault count: five vaults under one host budget reserve 32,768,000 B of page cache — exactly one default vault's worth — where the pre-#659 per-file constants would have reserved 163,840,000 B, a 5x reduction. Every one of the 10 handles still gets 3.28 MB, well above the 512 KiB floor. THE CAVEAT THAT MATTERS: reservations are not residency. Each additional mounted vault still costs ~10.1 MB of RSS at idle (connection state + bootstrap DDL, not the page cache, which SQLite fills lazily), so resident memory is still linear in vault count even though the budget is not. Measured on idle, freshly bootstrapped vaults that were never read — treat 10.1 MB as a floor.
_provenance.headroom: none — the ceilings ARE the host totals (DEFAULT_VAULT_FOOTPRINT), not observed + slack

_provenance.note: MEASURED by the #659 vault agent on a real run; cited, not re-derived. This is the audit's worst find (an hourly O(n^2) clustering pass) now bounded at the declared year-3 photo volume. It is a background sweep, so the owner-facing symptom is battery and a hot fan rather than a stalled screen — but at O(n^2) it was a stalled gateway.
